tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description opens with imperative phrasing ('Use this skill to assess...', 'Use it when a user asks...') and lists multiple explicit trigger contexts (outdated/EOL databases, upgrade failures, upgrade strategy questions, periodic audits) rather than describing internals. It is a single paragraph, dense but reasonably concise given the multi-engine scope it must cover, and focuses on user intent (what the user is asking about) while briefly summarizing output and the read-only guardrail.
tests.evidence: Use this skill to assess Amazon RDS and Aurora databases for major-version upgrade readiness across engines... Use it when a user asks which databases are outdated, end-of-life, approaching end of support, or on RDS Extended Support; why a past upgrade failed...

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body is dense but mostly consists of domain-specific procedures, non-obvious edge cases (Aurora de-dup, cross-engine precheck divergence), and specific AWS API calls rather than explanations of general concepts the agent would already know.
tests.evidence: An Aurora cluster is ONE database — do not also count its member instances... Aurora and RDS of the same community version can have DIFFERENT dates

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: Large tables (EOL calendars, findings classifications) are kept in references/ files and only linked conditionally; the body itself contains dispatch logic and brief inline rules (e.g., engine caveats) rather than full reference tables.
tests.evidence: Open the engine's calendar file (identified in Step 3). Read the engine's EOL calendar when classifying that engine's version — load [mysql/Aurora MySQL](references/mysql-eol-calendar.md)...

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: All 11 reference files are linked via markdown link syntax in the body.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link is accompanied by a specific trigger condition for when to load it (e.g., on engine detection, when classifying a version, when parsing evidence for a failed upgrade).
tests.evidence: Read [engine dispatch reference](references/engine-dispatch.md) when you first detect a database's `Engine`, to pick its calendar...

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths rooted at references/ with no absolute paths or traversals.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile, exact-sequence operations (version classification against calendar, finding classification, upgrade method ranking) are prescriptive, while advisory sections (strategy ranking rationale) explain why rather than dictating exact wording.
tests.evidence: Classify each finding ERROR / WARNING / NOTICE per that reference; never downgrade a level the engine reports.

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: Upgrade strategy methods are ranked with Blue/Green as the clear default/#1 choice, with in-place and snapshot-restore as alternates for specific scenarios, not presented as equal menu options.
tests.evidence: Rank #1 for production, Multi-AZ, or clustered/Aurora... Rank #1 only for non-prod single-AZ.

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable multi-phase procedure (discover, classify, analyze evidence, recommend strategy) applicable to any RDS/Aurora database rather than a one-off task.
tests.evidence: Phase 1 — Discover databases, config view, and version/EOL status... Phase 3 — Recommend an upgrade strategy

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill includes an explicit empirical gotcha about cross-engine precheck divergence plus numerous engine-specific caveats functioning as pitfalls.
tests.evidence: Cross-engine precheck divergence (EMPIRICAL — MySQL only, so far)... Treat such an Aurora WARNING as HIGH-PRIORITY action-required.
